name: Enterprise Digital Transformation Roadmap
description: A 36-month, value-gated enterprise transformation roadmap system that connects maturity gaps and priority use cases to target capabilities, architecture, operating model, investment gates, governance, and measurable outcomes.
style_guide:
# Value-Gated Enterprise Digital Transformation Roadmap

## Design intent

Create an executive roadmap that translates a transformation ambition into a governed 36-month sequence of capability, architecture, operating-model, and value releases. It must connect the north star to current maturity, prioritize use cases, describe the target data and technology spine, allocate investment by phase, define stage gates, and establish governance and value realization. The visual language should feel modern and operational: bright white canvas, near-black ink, emerald structure, cool-gray evidence fields, occasional warm exception color, refined serif conclusions, and precise sans-serif diagrams.

This template is specifically a maturity- and value-gated transformation roadmap. It is not a vendor solution proposal, a single-platform implementation plan, or a generic digital vision deck. Preserve the reference system, but never copy its company, factories, maturity scores, use cases, investment figures, architecture, targets, dates, or governance design. The previews are visual examples only; this guide is the authoring authority.

## Core visual signature

- Use white analytical pages with near-black or deep-navy type and emerald as the persistent transformation signal.
- Use a split cover with a large documentary operating image and clean editorial title field.
- Pair an elegant serif for outcome-led conclusions with a neutral grotesk for evidence and a mono face for phases, gates, metrics, and architecture labels.
- Favor maturity radars, capability maps, ranked use-case matrices, layered architecture diagrams, operating-model structures, stage-gated Gantts, and value scorecards.
- Use square panels, flat fills, fine cool-gray borders, and direct labels. Keep diagrams architecturally clean.
- Show links among capability, enabling platform, owner, phase, investment, KPI, and gate rather than presenting disconnected workstreams.

## Canvas, grid, and spacing

- Author on a fixed `1280 × 720 px` 16:9 canvas.
- Keep `64–72 px` side margins, `42–50 px` top navigation space, and `30–38 px` for sources and definitions.
- Use a 12-column grid with `18–22 px` gutters. Align capability layers, architecture rails, Gantt columns, metric rows, and governance panels.
- Reserve `120–165 px` for the page eyebrow and conclusion on analytical pages.
- Use `22–30 px` between major exhibits, `12–18 px` between related modules, and `8–10 px` between labels and values.
- Prefer balanced `6/6` current-and-target layouts, an `8/4` architecture-and-operating-model split, and full-width roadmaps.
- Keep enough white space that executive decisions remain distinct from technical detail.

## Color system

### Primary palette

- Transformation emerald: `#008A68`. Use for the north star, selected use cases, target capabilities, active architecture spine, approved phase, and value achieved.
- Near-black ink: `#121827`. Use for conclusions, body text, architecture labels, tables, and strong headers.
- Pure white: `#FFFFFF`. Use for the primary canvas, exhibit panels, and reversed text.
- Cool-gray field: `#EFF3F6`. Use for maturity areas, secondary layers, inactive roadmap phases, and contextual panels.
- Slate gray: `#66717F`. Use for body annotations, assumptions, sources, and inactive labels.
- Hairline gray: `#D8E0E6`. Use for borders, rules, radar grids, table separators, and timeline lanes.

### Semantic exceptions

- Decision orange: `#B75B00`. Use only for material gap, missed gate, risk, dependency, or decision required.
- Risk red: `#B64642`. Use only for severe exposure or failed control.
- Do not treat exception colors as template identity colors.

## Typography

- Use `Source Serif 4`, `Cormorant Garamond`, or a similar editorial serif for executive outcomes and page conclusions.
- Use `Inter`, `Arial`, or another neutral grotesk for capability, architecture, roadmap, governance, and KPI content.
- Use `IBM Plex Mono`, `Roboto Mono`, or a similar mono face for phase codes, gate criteria, maturity scores, metric definitions, dates, and source notes.
- Cover titles may be `52–66 px`; page conclusions `34–46 px`; body text `15–18 px`; technical labels `11–14 px`; key values `27–42 px`.
- Use emerald italic serif for at most one outcome phrase on a page.

## Persistent frame

- Use a compact section label at upper-left, page count at upper-right, and a thin near-black or emerald rule beneath.
- Carry phase names and time horizon consistently across capability, architecture, investment, and KPI pages.
- Add a quiet footer for baseline date, metric definition, architecture status, or source.
- Use consistent labels for baseline, target, committed, in flight, gated, realized, and at risk.

## Page archetypes

### Cover and transformation context

Use a split composition with a real operating-environment photograph on one side and a white title field on the other. Include the transformation horizon, sponsor, date, and one short outcome promise. Avoid generic technology imagery unrelated to the enterprise context.

### North star and current maturity

State the measurable north-star outcomes, not only technology ambition. Pair them with a six-dimension maturity radar or comparable diagnostic using defined levels and evidence dates. Show the few gaps that materially constrain value.

### Target capabilities and priority use cases

Build a layered capability map across customer, operations, data, technology, people, or another relevant model. Rank a limited set of use cases by value, feasibility, strategic fit, data readiness, and time to impact. Connect each priority use case to the capability it requires.

### Target architecture, data, and operating model

Use a layered target architecture with channels, applications, integration, data products, platforms, security, and infrastructure as appropriate. Make the data spine and governance visible. Pair it with transformation office, product pods, platform teams, and centers of excellence, including decision rights and ownership.

### Phased roadmap, investment, and gates

Use a 36-month Gantt grouped into foundation, scale, and optimize phases, or equivalent. Each phase must show deliverables, accountable owners, investment, dependencies, value release, and exit criteria. Stage gates should release the next tranche only when evidence is met.

### Governance, risk, and value measurement

Show executive, portfolio, product, and delivery cadences with clear decision rights. Use a value scorecard with baseline, target, current, owner, and reporting frequency. Add only the top risks and end with the exact steering-committee decisions required.

## Data and evidence integrity

- Never invent maturity scores, use-case value, investment, savings, revenue uplift, adoption, cycle time, architecture status, or risk exposure.
- Define maturity levels and cite diagnostic evidence; do not treat workshop opinion as measured performance without labeling it.
- Distinguish gross benefit, implementation cost, ongoing run cost, risk adjustment, timing, and realized value.
- Label architecture components as current, retained, modernized, replaced, proposed, or undecided.
- Use cases must show business owner, process scope, data readiness, dependency, baseline, target, and value method.
- Do not count deployed technology as adopted capability or booked benefit as realized value.
- Keep phase dates, financial periods, currencies, and scenario bases explicit.

## Imagery and iconography

- Use one documentary cover image of the actual operating environment, workforce, customer setting, or physical system.
- Body pages should prioritize diagrams, heatmaps, roadmaps, scorecards, and technical structures.
- Use a consistent minimal line-icon family for capability layers, data, platform, process, people, governance, and risk.
- Avoid glowing circuitry, abstract AI brains, holograms, stock server rooms, floating dashboards, and decorative app screenshots.

## Content rules

- Each page must connect one executive transformation question to measurable evidence and a decision.
- Keep vision, capability, use case, architecture, operating model, initiative, and KPI as distinct concepts.
- Make every roadmap item traceable to a business outcome or enabling dependency.
- Show what is intentionally deferred, not only what is in scope.
- Limit ordinary pages to one dominant model and no more than three supporting evidence groups.
- End with the next investment, prioritization, ownership, or risk decision.

## Avoid

- Do not reuse preview company facts, photos, maturity scores, use cases, systems, investments, targets, dates, or governance roles.
- Do not turn the template into a consulting solution proposal or a software-vendor architecture pitch.
- Do not confuse technical go-live with adoption, benefit realization, or maturity advancement.
- Do not create a roadmap made only of colored bars without deliverables, owners, dependencies, and gate criteria.
- Do not use emerald as a generic decoration on every object.
- Do not use gradients, glass effects, 3D diagrams, heavy shadows, oversized radii, or ornamental blobs.
- Do not repeat card grids; choose maturity, capability, architecture, roadmap, and governance structures according to the question.
